customManagers.description: Track web/buf.gen.yaml BSR codegen plugin pins via their inline `# renovate:` annotations

Track the Go buf.gen.yaml / buf.gen.internal.yaml BSR codegen plugin pins via their inline `# renovate:` annotations (holomush-9vyc3). Separate from the web manager: the patterns are root-anchored (`^buf.gen…`) so they exclude web/buf.gen.yaml and buf.gen.docs.yaml, the datasource is `go` (per-line via the annotation), and the version `v` prefix is captured into currentValue — Renovate's go versioning writes the bump back as `vX.Y.Z`, so capturing after `:v` (as the web manager does) would corrupt the pin to `:vvX.Y.Z`.

packageRules.description: Propose bumps of the go.mod `go` directive (depType golang). Renovate skips these by default (docs: modules/manager/gomod#updating-of-go-mod-and-toolchain-directives), but the required Vuln check runs govulncheck under the Go version setup-go reads from this directive, so a stdlib CVE fixed only in a newer 1.x patch leaves main red until the directive moves. groupName keeps the directive OUT of the all-non-major groups: PR #5014 showed a go 1.26 -> 1.27 bump riding that group and breaking every job (x/net drops http2.TrailerPrefix under go1.27 build tags). allowedVersions caps it below 1.27 until the pinned golangci-lint/staticcheck build (.custom-gcl.yml, honnef v0.7.0) supports Go 1.27 — it panics in buildir today; lift the cap together with that bump.

A go-directive MINOR bump (1.26.x -> 1.27.0) changes language semantics and can outrun the pinned golangci-lint/staticcheck build (.custom-gcl.yml), so it stays a manual merge; only patch bumps ride the gomod auto-merge rule above. Placed AFTER that rule on purpose: Renovate applies packageRules in order and the last matching rule wins, so this entry must come later to switch automerge back off for the go directive.
Batch all non-major npm/pnpm bumps into a single PR

Docs site (site/: bun + .bun-version) bumps get their own PR and are never auto-merged. The Starlight plugins are pre-1.0 (every minor is the breaking channel) and the site build (site.yml `Build site`) is NOT a required check, so inside the all-non-major group a broken docs build rode in unseen on PR #5014. A human runs `task docs:build` on this group's PR.
NATS packages — extra stabilization time, grouped, weekly schedule
Major version bumps require manual review

Group the web/buf.gen.yaml bufbuild/es pin with its @bufbuild/protoc-gen-es web/package.json devDependency so they bump together in one PR. Not auto-merged — a pin bump doesn't regenerate the committed _pb.ts stubs, so a human runs `task web:generate` on the bump PR (holomush-ai3o5).

Group the Go buf.gen.yaml / buf.gen.internal.yaml BSR codegen plugin pins with their go.mod runtimes so each bumps in lockstep: protocolbuffers/go↔google.golang.org/protobuf, connectrpc/go↔connectrpc.com/connect (both ship the generator in the runtime module, same version); protoc-gen-go-grpc tracks its own google.golang.org/grpc/cmd/protoc-gen-go-grpc submodule, independent of the google.golang.org/grpc runtime. Not auto-merged — a pin bump doesn't regenerate the committed *.pb.go stubs, so a human runs `task proto` on the bump PR. Last in the array so it overrides the broader gomod auto-merge and 'Google Go' grouping for these packages (holomush-9vyc3).

Hold typescript below 7 until the Svelte toolchain supports it standalone. TypeScript 7 support currently requires BOTH TypeScript 7 and TypeScript 6 installed in the project, plus the `--tsgo` or `--tsgo-experimental-api` flag — svelte-check hard-errors otherwise, which is what closed PR #4848. This is an ecosystem-readiness pin, not a repo defect. Issue #5000 is the trigger to REMOVE this rule; do not remove it before that issue confirms the toolchain is ready. `allowedVersions` rather than `enabled: false` so TypeScript 6 patch/minor updates keep flowing normally.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Group every outstanding vulnerability fix into ONE PR per base branch (default is one PR per dependency). The required Vuln check runs govulncheck over the whole module, so a per-dependency Go fix PR can never go green while any other reachable vuln remains in go.mod: 2026-08 to 2026-10 left 17 [SECURITY] PRs mutually blocked that way. Known trade-off: vulnerabilityAlerts cannot be scoped per manager, so npm/Docker security fixes ride the same PR; a red non-Go member holds the Go fixes until it is fixed or dropped.
